chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Moses (peace be upon him) supplicated, and Aaron (peace be upon him) said 'Ameen', and the Angels (peace be upon them) said 'Ameen'. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'Your supplication has been accepted, therefore be steadfast.'
And whoever fights in the Way of Allah, he will be answered, just as He answered for both of you, on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Moses' supplication regarding the acceptance of du'a for those who strive in God's path?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the prophetic tradition of 'tasmīn' (affirmation) by Aaron and the angels, establishing a divine precedent for the efficacy of collective supplication. It extends this spiritual principle to the concept of jihad, promising that those who strive in God's path will have their prayers answered on the Day of Judgment with the same certainty granted to Moses and Aaron, thereby linking physical struggle with spiritual acceptance.
